messages:
ana: FYI hit a nasty one during onboarding: our sampleapp kept authenticating with the old PROJECT key even after the ops sidecar injected the new ORG key into the pod env. Streaming connections kept alive with the old identity. anyone seen SDKs prefer cached creds over env updates?
kevin: interesting. which SDK and how are you rotating the envs?
ana: repro steps below:
```
# initial container image sets project key at build or from secret
export REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT=proj-111-old
# later, k8s sidecar updates env to org key after some bootstrap
export REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG=org-222-new
# start app
./start-sampleapp.sh
```
But requests indicate auth principal proj-111-old.
rita: oh yeah, older SDK versions write a local credential cache under ~/.redwood/credentials and the client init will prefer that file if present. If your container image baked that file or the process created it early, env rotations later don't take effect.
leo: that explains it. The rotation pattern in k8s we use patches the env at runtime, but processes that read creds at startup won't re-evaluate unless we restart them. For long-lived streams that reconnect, the cache can persist across reconnections.
ana: ouch. that matches exactly. I assumed env overrides file. big onboarding surprise for anyone using in-cluster injection.
kevin: UX options: 1) change precedence so environment variables always win, 2) detect mismatch at startup and emit a warning, or 3) offer an opt-in behavior to invalidate caches on SIGHUP.
rita: for a quick workaround, we added a tiny init script to our sampleapp container that removes ~/.redwood/credentials when REDWOOD_API_KEY_* is present. Not ideal but fixes it.
leo: longer term we should update SDK docs, add an integration test in sampleapp CI that asserts rotation semantics, and make a small CLI/SDK change to log a one-line warning when cached creds differ from env.
kevin: can someone open an issue with suggested priority and a proposed compatibility plan for SDK 1.x -> 2.x? We should avoid surprising existing users but still fix precedence.
devex-bot: Issue DEVEX-4598 created: "SDK cred precedence: env vs credential cache - rotation gotcha" linking to redwood/sdk and sampleapp repos.
rita: I'll draft the compatibility proposal: in 1.x emit the warning and document behavior; in 2.x flip precedence so env > file and add clear guidance in onboarding. Also add an explicit cache invalidation API.
nana: please also add a short note in the quickstart that says: "If you use injected env rotation in k8s, ensure no cached credentials are present in the container filesystem or restart processes after rotation." That would have saved us a 3am pager.
leo: assigning tasks: @rita for RFC + SDK PR (small change + unit test), @kevin to add e2e rotation test in sampleapp, @ana to update onboarding quickstart doc.
kevin: will add the e2e and a CI check. quick test idea: start sampleapp, swap env, assert outgoing requests flip principal within 30s.
nana: thanks all. patching our init script for now and will coordinate on the RFC. :relieved:
